title: Patch: `spec check` credits only a proof that runs: a TypeScript test or an SQL heading that is commented out no longer proves its ruling
thread:
**Issue #4851 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4851: Patch: `spec check` credits only a proof that runs: a TypeScript test or an SQL heading that is commented out no longer proves its ruling
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

`cargo jackioh spec check` (CLAUDE.md rule 3) passes a ruling whose only proof does not run, when that proof is a TypeScript test or an SQL heading that has been commented out or sits inside a string.

- `ts_test_titles` (`crates/tools/src/spec.rs:932-999`) scans the file's raw bytes for `it(`, `test(` and `describe(` titles.
- `sql_headings` (`:1045-1067`) finds `\echo` anywhere on a line.
- The Rust path blanks comments and strings first (`rust_code_only`, `:574`), and the module's own unit test refuses `// fn r999_commented() {}`.

With R1's only `proven_in` file holding any of these, `spec check` prints `1 rulings, 1 proofs … ok` and exits 0:

- `// it("R1 the fixture ruling holds", () => { … });`
- the same test inside `/* … */`
- `export const todo = 'write it("R1 the fixture ruling holds") one day';`
- `-- \echo '### R1: the fixture ruling ###'` in an SQL script

No live instance exists today: a grep of every TypeScript file under the citing roots for a commented `it`, `test` or `describe` with an R-id found none. The hole is that the next one would pass.

### What should happen

`spec/README.md`, Note format: "`proven_in` lists the files whose tests prove it, and only a test that runs counts (#1718)", and a TypeScript title counts "as long as no `.skip`, `.todo`, `.fixme` or `.only` turns it off".

### How to reproduce

Two tests fail on `main` (3a83bd7), in [`crates/tools/tests/audit_tools.rs` at b5a9801](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/b5a9801/crates/tools/tests/audit_tools.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`): `spec_check_refuses_a_typescript_proof_that_is_commented_out` and `spec_check_refuses_an_sql_heading_that_is_commented_out`.

Each builds a small tree in a scratch directory (`spec/rulings/R0001.md` with `id: R1`, `cards: "issue #1"` and one `proven_in`; `crates/cards/catalog.json` as `{}`; the proof file), runs `jackioh spec --root <tree> check`, asserts that a control with a live test passes, and then asserts each dead proof is refused.

Run with `JACKIOH_AUDIT_TMP=<a scratch directory> cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit --test audit_tools`.

Output today:

```
R1's only proof is no test that runs, yet `spec check` passed:
line-comment: // it("R1 the fixture ruling holds", …) -> spec check: 1 rulings, 1 proofs, 1 citations in 1 files, 0 links: ok
block-comment: … ok        string: … ok        sql-comment: -- \echo '### R1: the fixture ruling ###' … ok
```

### Where

CI, deploys or tooling: `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` (`ts_test_titles`, `sql_headings`, `proves`).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Before `ts_test_titles` scans, blank `//` and `/* */` comments and the contents of strings and template literals, keeping the title string that directly follows `it(`, `test(` or `describe(`. In `sql_headings`, skip an `\echo` on a line whose text before it starts with `--`.
- Run the fixed check over the real repository and say in the pull request that it still passes (it should: no live case was found). If it does not, the rulings it now flags need real proofs, not an exemption.
- Deliberate today, so not part of this: an empty or all-skipped `describe("R1 …")` counts, and the unit test `refuses_a_typescript_title_that_does_not_run` asserts `describe("R1 after", () => {})` proves R1.
- Contrived Rust neighbours, confirmed on a fixture and left for the builder's judgement: a `#[test] fn r1_…` inside a `macro_rules!` body that is never invoked, under `#[cfg(any())]`, or with `#[cfg_attr(all(), ignore)]` counts as a proof though it never runs.
- The tests belong beside the module's existing unit tests in `spec.rs` (it already builds fixture trees) rather than in a new integration file.

Found by an audit of the project's own gates (`crates/tools`); the reproductions were run and the code read before filing.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45598487025)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Close the `spec check` proof hole so a TypeScript proof inside a `//` or `/* */` comment or inside a string/template literal no longer proves its ruling, and an SQL `\echo` heading commented out with `--` no longer proves its ruling. A live `it`/`test`/`describe` title and a live `\echo` heading keep proving exactly as today.

## Files to touch

| Path | New / change | What changes there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` | change | `ts_test_titles` becomes comment- and string-aware; `sql_headings` skips `--`-commented headings; two new unit tests in its `tests` module |
| `spec/README.md`, `spec/rulings/`, `spec/pending/`, `spec/history/`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md` | touch none | No new ruling and no doc change: `spec/README.md` Note format already requires that only a test that runs counts (#1718); this change enforces it |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/ai/`, or `apps/web/src/wire/`. Governing text: `spec/README.md` Note format (`proven_in`, #1718) and CLAUDE.md rule 3.

## Steps

1. Re-read `spec/README.md` Note format and `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` lines 940–1115 (`ts_test_titles`, `ts_call_end`, `sql_headings`, `sql_heading_names`, `proves`) before editing.
2. In `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`, rewrite the `while` loop of `ts_test_titles` so the `it`/`test`/`describe` keyword search only fires in code. At the top of each iteration, before the keyword match, add three skips on the raw `bytes`: if `bytes[i..]` starts with `//`, advance `i` to the next `\n` (or end) and `continue`; if it starts with `/*`, advance past the first following `*/` (TS comments do not nest, unlike `block_comment_end`) and `continue`; if `bytes[i]` is `"`, `'` or `` ` ``, advance past the matching quote handling `\` escapes (`i += 1; while bytes[i] != quote { if bytes[i] == b'\\' { i += 1; } i += 1; } i += 1`) and `continue`. Leave the rest of the function unchanged: the `.modifier` loop, the `SKIPPED_TS_MODIFIERS` check, the `ts_call_end` skip of disabled groups, and the title read between the quotes that directly follow the call's `(`. This blanks comments and non-title strings while keeping the title string, per the issue's notes. Copy the escape/comment idiom from `ts_call_end` in the same file.
3. In `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`, fix `sql_headings` so a commented heading is skipped: for each `\echo` at byte offset `at`, compute the line start as `src[..at].rfind('\n').map(|p| p + 1).unwrap_or(0)`, take `before = src[line_start..at]`, and if `before.trim_start().starts_with("--")` skip that occurrence (advance `rest` past the `\echo` and `continue` without pushing). All other `\echo '### … ###'` / `'=== … ==='` handling stays as is.
4. Add unit test `refuses_a_typescript_proof_in_comments_and_strings` in the `tests` module next to `refuses_a_typescript_title_that_does_not_run`: assert `ts_test_titles` on `"// it(\"R1 line commented\", () => {});\n"` returns empty; on `"/* it(\"R1 block commented\", () => {}); */"` returns empty; on `"export const todo = 'write it(\"R1 one day\") someday';\n"` and the `/* … */` and double-quote/template variants returns empty; assert `!proves("a.test.ts", <each dead src>, 1)` and `proves("a.test.ts", "it(\"R1 live\", () => {});\n", 1)`. Use only `R1` (note `spec/rulings/R0001.md` exists) so rule 3 still passes on this file.
5. Add unit test `refuses_an_sql_heading_that_is_commented_out` next to `credits_an_sql_proof_only_from_a_heading`: assert `!proves("x.sql", "-- \\echo '### R1: the fixture ###'\n", 1)` and `!proves("x.sql", "  -- \\echo '### R1: the fixture ###'\n", 1)` (leading whitespace still commented), and `proves("x.sql", "\\echo '### R1: the fixture ###'\n", 1)` for the live control.
6. Run the checks in Tests below, then run the fixed check over the real repository and confirm it still passes with no new problems (a grep found no live commented case, so any newly flagged ruling needs a real proof, never an exemption).

## Tests

- `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`, `refuses_a_typescript_proof_in_comments_and_strings`: line-comment, block-comment, single/double-quote and template-literal dead `it("R1 …")` proofs are refused (`proves` false, `ts_test_titles` empty); a live `it("R1 live")` still proves.
- `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`, `refuses_an_sql_heading_that_is_commented_out`: `-- \echo '### R1: … ###'` (with and without leading spaces) is refused; a line-initial `\echo` still proves.
- Keep existing `reads_typescript_test_titles`, `refuses_a_typescript_title_that_does_not_run` (including `describe("R1 after", () => {})` proving R1), and `credits_an_sql_proof_only_from_a_heading` green unchanged.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Each of the four dead proofs from the issue (line comment, block comment, string-held title, `-- \echo`) is refused while its live control passes.
- [ ] The two new unit tests fail without the fix and pass with it.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` over the real repository all pass.
- [ ] No file outside `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` changed; no test ignored, deleted, or weakened; no new ruling note or pending file added.
- [ ] The pull request states the real-repository `spec check` result.

## Risks

- Template literals with `${ … }` containing a real `it(` call would be skipped as string content; no such proof exists in the tree, and the issue's blanking prescription accepts this.
- TS block comments end at the first `*/` (they do not nest); do not copy the Rust nested `block_comment_end` for this scan.
- The empty or all-skipped `describe("R<n> …")` still counts, and the Rust `macro_rules!` / `cfg(any())` / `cfg_attr(all(), ignore)` neighbours still count; all are deliberate and out of scope, so do not "fix" them.
- New tests must cite only R ids that have notes (`R1` is safe); a literal `R999`-style id in this file would itself fail rule 3.

## Open questions

None. Difficulty is medium: one crate's tooling plus its unit tests, no engine, AI, cross-crate, migration, or large change.
````
